Daily Devotional

December 2

18 Pride goeth before destruction, and an haughty spirit before a fall. (Proverbs 16:18 KJV)

What a tremendous truth this is, as people who get carried away with pride, are always setting themselves up for a failure. Pride is one of the most deadly of all sins we can have, as when you put yourself ahead of others and become full of pride, then you are asking for failure. God can humble the proud, and exalt the humble, as shown many times in the bible. You can’t be carried away with pride, and obey the commands that Jesus gave, to love God above all, and others as yourself (Matthew 22:37-40). Jesus said “if you love me, you will follow my commands” (John 14:15), and you must obey Jesus to assure your eternal salvation (Hebrews 5:9). Pride is being self-centered, and thinking only of what you want. It is a predominant problem in this world today, as we are living in the “me” generation, where it is all about us, and what we want. It is directly opposed to what Jesus taught, and shows how much the devil is in control of our world, as it is today. Put others first, and live the life that Jesus instructed us to live, and reap the benefits of God’s blessings in your life. Praise God for His goodness!

People, who get totally caught up in them selves, with a haughty spirit, are setting themselves up for a fall. You should never think more highly of yourself, than what you truly are, as that goes against all the teachings of Jesus. These traits of pride and haughtiness are so common in the world today that they are even promoted, and we are told that we need to have great self-esteem, and be proud. We teach our kids from a young age, to be proud of their accomplishments. The world today does not relate to this verse, and does not think it is true, but it is, and we need to take care not to let ourselves get into pride and self. As long as we put others before ourselves, as the bible teaches (Philippians 2:3), then we will stay away from the destruction and fall that this verse is talking about. Follow the example of the Lord, and stay humble (Matthew 11:29), and full of God’s kind of love. To be full of God, you have to be full of love, as God is Love (1 John 4:8).

Devotional by Pastor Joe W. Green, www.Infinite-Faith.com
